gaps.sentence: He ___ to the reporters that the deal was off.
gaps.explanation: 'Said to the reporters that...' is correct; tell cannot be followed by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the thermostat,' the technician warned us. The technician warned us ___ the thermostat.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands are reported with 'warned + object + not to + infinitive'.

gaps.sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).

gaps.sentence: 'Please don't leave until the lights are off,' the caretaker begged us. The caretaker begged ___ until the lights were off.
gaps.explanation: Begging somebody not to do something uses object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: "Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
